prompt: This verse clearly indicate that.........

options.text: Other religion will be accepted as long as you practice with pure heart.
The religion of Islam is correct but you can choose from ur desired religion.
Allah (S.W.T) is forcing his servant, that is (humans ) to accept Islam as their religion because other religions will be rejected.
The religion of Islam is the correct way and other religions will not be accepted.

explanation: The original embedded verse is Quran 3:85. In the course interpretation it concerns acceptance of religion, not a license to force belief. Keep it distinct from Quran 2:256 and from judgments about particular people’s access or culpability.

distractorExplanations.B: Personal preference is not the criterion expressed by the verse.
distractorExplanations.C: A claim about acceptance does not itself authorize coercion.

subject: religion
topic: Divine attributes and justice
chapter: Religion Review §17: Divine attributes and justice
prompt: As far as the positive attributes of Allah the Almighty is concerned, which of the following is the best answer?

options.text: Positive attributes in fact is not a good term for His Attributes.
There is no difference between the positive and negative attributes both of them are the same.
The positive attributes are those attributes which represent one perfection of the perfects of Allah the Almighty.

explanation: Positive attributes affirm a perfection; negative attributes deny a deficiency. These are distinct classifications, not good versus bad attributes of God.

distractorExplanations.A: Positive is a usable technical classification in this account.
distractorExplanations.B: Affirmation of perfection and denial of deficiency are not identical forms of predication.
distractorExplanations.D: The definition of positive attributes is supplied in C.

prompt: From the Islamic point of view the followers of other religions;

Will be punished and sent to Hell.

topic: One revealed core, successive laws, final prophethood
chapter: Religion Review §18: One revealed core, successive laws, final prophethood
prompt: From the Islamic point of view;

options.text: There are three divine religions and all of them are true and valid for ever.
There is only one religion which is called Islam and the differences between Prophets were in Sharia.
The name of religion is not important. We must only try to be a good doer in our life.
Any nation can have its own religion.

explanation: The course describes one revealed core of submission to God while locating differences among missions in practical prescriptions. This is its framework, not an assertion of identical doctrines everywhere.

distractorExplanations.A: This erases the course’s distinction between earlier and final applicable dispensations.
distractorExplanations.C: Conduct matters, but the technical definition does not dispense with beliefs.
distractorExplanations.D: The course does not ground revealed guidance simply in national preference.

prompt: When we say that Allah s.w.t is All- seeing or All- hearing, what do we mean?

options.text: Obviously it means that Allah s.w.t has the eyes to see and the ear to hear.

prompt: Which of the following is not from the signs of truthfulness of a religion?

options.text: If it is predicted by previous one

explanation: The number of adherents does not by itself establish that a religion’s claims are true. Proposed rationality, preservation or prediction criteria still require their own evidence.

distractorExplanations.A: The course treats rational assessability as relevant rather than mere head count.
distractorExplanations.C: Preservation is among the criteria discussed, though it alone is not sufficient proof.
distractorExplanations.D: A prediction claim can be assessed textually; it must not simply be assumed.

prompt: According to one of the traditions, Imam Ali a.s defines “justice” as follows:

options.text: Justice means to give the things to everybody equally.

chapter: Religion Review §18: One revealed core, successive laws, final prophethood
prompt: One of the reasons that all religions are one and united is:

options.text: Because they are according to the nature of man and the nature of man is one.
Because Prophet Ibrahim is the father of all Prophets.
Because all of us are human being and must follow Prophet Adam (pbuh)

explanation: The course’s unity argument connects guidance with a shared human nature. This is a premise within its theological account, not a claim that every historical doctrine is identical.

distractorExplanations.B: The assertion that Abraham is father of all prophets is not the stated nature-based argument.
distractorExplanations.C: A general appeal to following Adam does not give the stated reasoning about shared nature.
distractorExplanations.D: The shared-nature premise is supplied in A.
